text: Every pipeline so far has been a definition — code that exists somewhere. Here's how that code actually becomes a running pipeline, deployed on purpose and repeatably, plus Chapter 3's close.
Databricks Asset Bundles are Databricks' own YAML-based deployment tool. A resources.pipelines entry in databricks.yml declares a pipeline as code, pointing at Lesson 13's table definitions.
Lesson 53 already covered triggered versus continuous in full. The continuous field in a bundle is where that choice actually lives — set once, deployed with everything else.
Chapter 3 covered Lakeflow's declarative model, the real SQL and Python syntax, the honest trade-off against a notebook, Expectations' SQL side, and now deployment as code.
Chapter 3 is complete. Chapter 4, Jobs, Workflows & Orchestration, picks up where Lesson 54 left off — Jobs, the Workflows UI, task dependencies, and cluster choices.
